title: Food Spoilage — Cereals, Pulses, Oils, Fruits, Vegetables and Canned Foods
shortDescription: Mould, insects, enzymes and canning failures: the full spoilage map for plant foods.
genZNote: Dry foods fail by mould, wet foods by bacteria, cans by sneaky spore-formers. Flat sour vs hard swell is the question that keeps coming back.

sections.heading: Cereals, Pulses and Oils
bullets: Cereals/pulses: moulds (Aspergillus, Penicillium, Fusarium) when moisture is high; mycotoxins; bread ropiness by Bacillus subtilis/licheniformis; insects and rodents (weevils, borers, khapra beetle).
Oils: hydrolytic rancidity (lipase from moulds/bacteria) and oxidative rancidity (O2, light, metals).
Control: dry to safe moisture (about 12% for cereals, lower for oilseeds/pulses), fumigation, hermetic or cold storage, antioxidants.

sections.heading: Fruits and Vegetables
bullets: Fruits: acidic, so yeasts and moulds dominate — Penicillium (blue/green mould, patulin), Botrytis (grey mould), Rhizopus (soft rot).
Vegetables: higher pH — bacterial soft rot (Erwinia, Pseudomonas) and fungal rots; enzymatic softening by pectinases; physiological damage (chilling injury, ethylene-triggered ripening, bruising).
Control: low temperature, controlled atmosphere, sanitising washes, minimal handling, drying, canning and freezing.

sections.heading: Spoilage of Canned Foods
sections.body: Can swells: flipper, springer, soft swell, hard swell. Underprocessing, leaker contamination and thermophilic growth in warm storage are the three main causes. The commercial sterility concept (12D botulinum cook) guides low-acid canning.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Spoilage of plant foods arises from moulds, bacteria, enzymes, insects and physiological changes, and canned-food spoilage reflects thermal underprocessing or leakage.

highYieldFacts: Low-acid canned foods need pressure retorting; acid foods can be hot-filled.
commonTraps: Do not say flat sour produces gas.
